input.quote: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.1 already secures our ownership of Customer Data and independently owned IP, limits Vendor to processing that material solely to provide, secure, support and improve the Services (service delivery, not independent exploitation), and 14.4 rules out unilateral joint ownership; 14.3 preserves Vendor Technology ownership and routes embedded Vendor Technology to the perpetual 13.2 licence. The failure is 14.2: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for us while our only licence is revocable, non-transferable and expires with the Order Form term. That fails the fallback (no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables) — we lose access to bespoke reports, configurations and integrations we paid for at term end. We take the fallback rather than preferred, leaving Vendor's ownership of Deliverables and its generic tools and know-how intact, and simply upgrade the licence sentence.

mappings.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
mappings.quote: No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.

proposal.summary: Replace the revocable, term-limited Deliverable licence in 14.2 with a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables for Customer's business.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 14.2 gives us only a revocable, non-transferable licence expiring with the Order Form term in work product we paid to have created. We have left Vendor's ownership of Deliverables and its Vendor Technology intact and taken our fallback position instead: a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables for our business.

ops.oldText: Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify, and sublicense each Deliverable for its business.
